concerns.text: Task T005 adds a uniform GPU fallback for generation. This directly violates NFR‑001 (≤60 s inference on a CPU‑only free‑tier runner) and FR‑002, which require the pipeline to run on CPU‑only hardware. Introducing GPU execution weakens the non‑functional constraint.

Task T006 only verifies surface entities via regex and AST checks. FR‑006 requires verification of *any* technical term generated by the LLM against the repository codebase, including intent‑related terms. The task does not address verification of technical‑intent entities, leaving FR‑006 unsatisfied.

SC‑002 mandates measuring that ≥90 % of dataset entries are successfully generated across all three models. No task records this success‑rate metric or asserts it in verification, so the acceptance criterion is missing.

The Constitution (III. Data Hygiene) requires checksums for all data files and that no transformation modifies data in place. None of the tasks (e.g., T003, T004, T005, T006, T007, T008) compute or record checksums, nor do they enforce creation of new files for each transformation, violating the data‑hygiene principle.

Constitution I (Reproducibility) demands that random seeds be pinned for all stochastic components (zero‑shot classifier, model generation, Monte‑Carlo power analysis). The task list contains no explicit step to set or document seeds, risking non‑reproducible results.
